sections.h2: What is Bryan County, Georgia like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Bryan County sits in the Savannah metropolitan area and is split in two by the Fort Stewart military installation. Pembroke, the county seat, sits in the rural north. Richmond Hill, the biggest city, is a Savannah suburb in the south, and Wikipedia points out that a public-road trip between them leaves the county (Wikipedia). That divide is why the county keeps two offices for nearly every property tax service.

Bryan became a county on December 19, 1793. It counted 44,738 people in 2020, and QuickFacts puts mid-2025 at 52,062, up 16.4 percent from the 2020 base. Homes are valued at a median $343,200 and household income is a median $103,408, the highest figures of the four counties in the Census QuickFacts comparison. Builders pulled 733 permits in 2025.

The Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America electric vehicle plant began production in 2024 and is the county's largest employer.

sections.h2: Where are the Bryan County property tax offices?
sections.html:
The assessor and the tax commissioner each run one office in Pembroke and one in Richmond Hill. Values come from the assessor. Billing, collection and distribution belong to the commissioner. By its own account, the assessor's side neither sets the rate nor collects a dollar.

sections.h2: What are the Bryan County due dates and late charges?
sections.html:
For tax year 2026, bills were mailed on October 16 with a due date of Tuesday, December 15, 2026. The county's property tax page says bills generally go out around September and give at least 60 days to pay, so the date can shift from year to year.

Here is the county's published schedule for late payment:

  • Interest runs at 0.875 percent per month, or fraction of a month, beginning the day following the deadline.
  • At 120 days past due, a 5 percent penalty is tacked on.
  • Each further 120 days adds another 5 percent, with 20 percent as the ceiling.
  • A bill 30 days delinquent lets the tax commissioner, serving as ex-officio sheriff, start tax sale proceedings.

Under Georgia law the January 1 owner of record stays on the bill for the year, and the office asks for the recorded deed once a sale closes.

sections.h2: How is a Bryan County home valued and how is an appeal made?
sections.html:
The assessor sets fair market value, and 40 percent of it, minus any homestead exemption, becomes the taxable value. The commissioner then applies the millage rate. The county has posted the 2026 millage rates on its tax page.

Notices for 2026 went out on June 12, and the final day to appeal was July 27. That window is shut, and the assessor's page says late appeals are refused. Its rules are worth knowing for any later year:

  • Use the county's written appeal form.
  • Get it physically to the Pembroke or Richmond Hill office before 5:00 p.m. on deadline day.
  • Nothing sent by email or fax is accepted, and a postmark proves nothing.

The assessor's staff are also photographing homes to refresh records, so a county vehicle may pause outside yours. After a sale, the new owner sees a value the following year, when the first notice arrives.

sections.h2: Who is billed when a Bryan County house changes hands?
sections.html:
The commissioner's page says the office does not prorate taxes according to the date of sale, the amount of usage or current ownership. Any split between buyer and seller therefore happens at the closing table.

Once you sell, give the tax commissioner the recorded deed and closing papers so the next bill finds the new owner. Leave them at either office, mail them to P.O. Box 447, Pembroke, GA 31321, or email propertytax@bryancountyga.gov. Address changes and homestead applications belong with the assessor.

Find out from your closing attorney how this year's bill will be shared and whether the December deadline lands before your closing. For any open bill, get a payoff figure from the commissioner so it can come out of the sale.

sections.h2: How do schools and housing vary across Bryan County?
sections.html:
Bryan County School District covers kindergarten through twelfth grade everywhere except parts of Fort Stewart, where elementary students go to schools run by the Department of Defense Education Activity. Older students from the base attend county public schools.

The numbers describe a young, family-heavy county. In 2020, 28.9 percent of residents were under 18, the median age was 35.5 and 44.8 percent of households had children. QuickFacts adds 16,603 households averaging 2.90 people, 77.7 percent owner occupancy and a median gross rent of $1,618.

  • Pembroke and the north end are mostly rural, and parcels there tend to be larger.
  • Richmond Hill and the south end sit in the Savannah commuter zone, with newer subdivisions.
  • Fort Stewart separates the two ends, so owners in each part usually use the closer tax office.

Go to whichever location is closer, since both handle the same tax matters.

sections.h2: What about homestead, mobile homes and business property in Bryan County?
sections.html:
The county's sample calculation uses a $2,000 homestead reduction from assessed value. Applications go to the assessor, and your status on January 1 decides eligibility, so ask that office which exemptions match your age, income or veteran status.

Mobile homes are billed under their own rules. Without a homestead exemption, the bill arrives in January and is due April 1. With one, the home is taxed along with its land, and that bill is due around November 15. Taxes must be paid, with a receipt in hand, before any mobile home is moved, even out of the county.

A business must file a personal property return with the assessor by April 1 in every year it operates, and state-set values apply if it does not. Timber sales go on Department of Revenue form PT-283T, and heavy-duty equipment bought from a dealer is taxed in its purchase year.

faqs.q: What is the 2026 due date for Bryan County property tax?
faqs.a: The 2026 bills carry a due date of Tuesday, December 15, 2026, and were mailed on October 16. After the due date, interest of 0.875 percent per month applies.

faqs.q: Is it too late to appeal a 2026 Bryan County assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. The 2026 cutoff was 5:00 p.m. on July 27, and the assessor's office refuses late appeals. Watch for the next notice and file in writing within 45 days of its date.

faqs.q: Does Bryan County split property tax by sale date?
faqs.a: No. The commissioner's office says it does not prorate by sale date, so the buyer and seller settle the bill between them at closing.

faqs.q: Where should the deed go after a Bryan County sale?
faqs.a: Send the recorded deed and closing documents to the Bryan County Tax Commissioner, P.O. Box 447, Pembroke, GA 31321, or to propertytax@bryancountyga.gov. You can also drop them at the Pembroke or Richmond Hill office.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay Bryan County property tax?
faqs.a: Interest and penalties accumulate, and penalties stop at 20 percent. Once a bill is 30 days delinquent the commissioner may start tax sale proceedings, so call early if you cannot pay in full.
